content.text: A charged particle moves at right angles to a uniform magnetic field in a vacuum. The particle moves in a circle with period
. An identical particle enters the same field at right angles with
What is the period of the motion of the second particle?
Thinks the radius does not change; the same circle is traversed at twice the speed: T/2
Sees that the radius doubles but forgets that the speed also increases (T ∝ r): 2T
Thinks the radius increases as v² (r ∝ v², a wrong deduction from the expression mv²/r) and forgets the increase in speed: 4T

qvB = mv²/r → r = mv/(qB). T = 2πr/v = 2πm/(qB): the period is independent of speed. When the speed doubles the radius also doubles; the circumference and the speed increase in the same proportion, so the period does not change.

document.outcome: Undeflected passage through perpendicular electric and magnetic fields (v = E/B)

content.text: A beam of electrons passes between two parallel plates that are 2.0 cm apart. The potential difference between the plates is 600 V. A uniform magnetic field of strength 1.5 mT is applied at right angles to both the electric field and the beam. The electrons pass between the plates without being deflected.
What is the speed of the electrons?
Does not convert the plate separation to metres: E = 600 / 2.0 = 300; 300 / 1.5 × 10⁻³ = 2.0 × 10⁵
Uses the potential difference instead of the field strength (v = V/B): 600 / 1.5 × 10⁻³ = 4.0 × 10⁵
E = V/d = 600 / 0.020 = 3.0 × 10⁴ V m⁻¹. No-deflection condition: eE = evB → v = E/B = 3.0 × 10⁴ / 1.5 × 10⁻³ = 2.0 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹.

document.outcome: Direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor (F = BIL sin θ)

content.text: A straight horizontal wire lies in the plane of the page and carries a current directed towards the right of the page. The wire is in a uniform magnetic field that is directed
What is the direction of the magnetic force on the wire?

stimuli.description: A horizontal wire in the plane of the page, running from left to right, with a current arrow (I) pointing right along it. The region around the wire is filled with ⊗ symbols showing a uniform magnetic field into the page. The "top of the page" is perpendicular to the wire and in the plane of the page. Diagram not to scale.

content.text: towards the top of the page
towards the bottom of the page
Applies the rule with the wrong hand, or takes the direction of electron flow instead of the current direction
Thinks the force is in the direction opposite to the field
Thinks the force is in the direction of the field (confusion with F = qE in an electric field)

Rule used: the right-hand rule, F = IL × B (conventional current direction). Axes: x to the right, y to the top of the page, z out of the page. Current +x, field −z: (+x) × (−z) = +y. The force is towards the top of the page. (Fleming's left-hand rule gives the same result: forefinger = field = into the page, middle finger = current = to the right, thumb = force = up.)

document.outcome: Motion of a charged particle in a uniform electric field

content.text: An electron enters a region of uniform electric field in a vacuum. The initial velocity of the electron is at right angles to the electric field lines. There is no magnetic field.
Which describes the path of the electron in the field and the speed of the electron?
The path is a circular arc and the speed is constant.
Confuses the electric field with a magnetic field (thinks the force is always perpendicular to the velocity)
The path is a circular arc and the speed increases.
Thinks the path is a circle as in a magnetic field, but correctly thinks that the field transfers energy
The path is a parabola and the speed increases.
The path is a parabola and the speed is constant.
Path correct; but considers only the velocity component perpendicular to the field, or says "the force is initially perpendicular to the velocity, so it does no work"

The electric force is constant in magnitude and direction (parallel to the field lines, opposite to the field). The velocity component perpendicular to the field is unchanged and the component along the field increases uniformly: the path is a parabola (like horizontal projectile motion). The force has a component along the direction of motion, so it does work; the speed increases.
